title: DataCite
version: 2026-10 faithful rebuild (Public Data Files 2023, 2024, 2025; PID Links 2023, May 2025)
cite_as: DataCite (2023-2025). DataCite Public Data File. https://datafiles.datacite.org/
description: The **DataCite Public Data Files** (CC0) as one range-queryable graph: **109,263,993 DOI records**, one per DOI, and the **PID Graph** (613,426,534 relation events from the 2023 and May 2025 PID Links files), reified as provenance-bearing `dcite:PidRelation`s. Converted by `scripts/datacite/parquet_to_nt.py`; the converter wrote 10,961,620,937 statements.
## What is in it

- One `dcite:Resource` per DOI at `https://doi.org/{doi}`, typed by its resourceTypeGeneral (all 32 DataCite 4.6 values), with title, publisher, publication year, dates, version, language, landing page, usage metrics (2024+), subjects, reified creators (a `dcite:AgentRole` with the name and affiliations the record gives, held by an `https://orcid.org/` agent when the ORCID is valid), funders (`dcite:fundedBy`) and DOI-typed related identifiers as typed edges.

- The PID Graph: every event is a direct typed edge **and** a `dcite:PidRelation` `<{subject}/event/{uuid}>` with one `relationSubject`, `relationObject`, exact `relationType`, `assertedBy` (the source) and `occurredAt`. Events from both PID Links files are kept; an event (uuid) present in both is taken once, from May 2025.

- Funding: `dcite:fundedBy` links a record to its funder (ROR, Crossref Funder ID, or a record-scoped IRI when the record gives no usable id); what the record says about the funder (`dcite:funderName`, an id not minted) sits on its `dcite:FundingReference`, never on the shared funder IRI.
- Works key by DOI and people by ORCID, so the graph joins crossref, opencitations, openaire, dblp, zenodo and orcid by IRI.
## One record per DOI, and where it came from

DataCite published three snapshots. Each DOI is converted **once**, from the newest file that has it (R9), and within one file from the row with the latest `updated` (R10: 728 DOIs in 2024, 3 in 2025). `dcite:fromSnapshot` says which file:
- `dcite:snapshot-2025`: 108,468,903 records
- `dcite:snapshot-2024`: 308,793 records whose DOI is not in the 2025 file
- `dcite:snapshot-2023`: 486,297 records whose DOI is in neither later file
Filter with `?r dcite:fromSnapshot dcite:snapshot-2025` for the 2025 state only.
## Conversion rules and what each did

The principle is **faithfulness**: the graph says what DataCite says. An identifier is rewritten only when the rewrite is deterministic and names the same thing (`https://doi.org/10.x/y` is the DOI `10.x/y`); anything that cannot be made a valid IRI that way is **dropped and counted**, never guessed. Literals are never cleaned. Counts are occurrences, summed over all five files.
| Rule | What it does | Rescued | Encoded | Kept as text | Dropped |

| R0 | One identity per DOI: the registered string, ASCII whitespace trimmed, lower-cased, nothing else. Plan, record IRI and pointers share it; a record's own DOI never goes through R1. The build refuses two registered DOIs on one IRI. | 0 | 0 | 6 | 0 |

| R1 | One DOI normaliser for related identifiers, funder ids and link endpoints: strip doi.org URL prefixes, `doi:`, `doi/`, `org/`, a leading `%20` / `%7C%5D`, spaces in the `10.NNNN` prefix; lower-case. A registered DOI is left untouched. | 173,978,232 | 0 | 42 | 0 |

| R2 | Percent-encode what RFC 3987 forbids (`[ ]`, a second `#`, a stray `%`, U+FFFD, C1, private-use) as `rete export --sanitize-iris` does; oxiri then checks every IRI and one it rejects is dropped. | 0 | 212,554 | 0 | 0 |
| R3 | Funder IRI: ROR (check digits must pass) > Crossref Funder ID (also a bare Funder Registry number) > a record-scoped `<doi>/funder/<sha1(name)>`. | 13 | 0 | 200,193 | 0 |
| R4 | An empty or `#PLACEHOLDER_PARENT_METADATA_VALUE#` funder name is no name; a reference with neither name nor usable id is dropped. | 0 | 0 | 0 | 20 |
| R5 | A link endpoint with no scheme is rescued by R1 or dropped with its event; a URL the IRI parser rejects is dropped. | 48 | 0 | 0 | 247 |

| R6 | `hdl:` -> `https://hdl.handle.net/`. `https://orcid.org/` only when the mod 11-2 check digit passes; a creator's failing ORCID is `dcite:rawIdentifier`, a failing link URL is kept verbatim. | 14,666 | 0 | 14,544 | 0 |

| R7 | All 38 DataCite 4.6 relationType values have their own property for metadata and links; `is-funded-by` is `dcite:fundedBy`; other link types are `dcite:isRelatedTo` with the exact type on the PidRelation. | 20,048,535 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| R8 | A DOI-typed related identifier with no DOI after R1 is dropped; an embedded DOI is taken only when exactly one stands there, delimited. | 0 | 0 | 0 | 1,204,136 |
| R9 | One record per DOI: 2025 wins, else 2024, else 2023; `dcite:fromSnapshot` names the file. | 0 | 0 | 0 | 124,087,770 |
| R10 | Within one file, the row with the latest `updated` wins. | 0 | 0 | 0 | 731 |
| R11 | `occurredAt` `0000-01-01` is not emitted. A publicationYear outside 1000-2027 is `dcite:publicationYearText`. | 0 | 0 | 271,014 | 13,947 |
| R12 | `landingPage` is `xsd:anyURI` only when it parses as an IRI, else a plain string. | 0 | 0 | 10,624 | 0 |
| R13 | Literals as DataCite has them: no trimming, normalisation or mojibake repair; C0 controls written as `\u` escapes. | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| R14 | `rorId` only when the ROR check digits pass; otherwise `dcite:rawIdentifier`. | 51,705 | 0 | 8,438 | 0 |

| R15 | Under `10.13039/` a DOI is `10.13039/<digits>`: a value naming exactly one Funder Registry number (`10.13039/http://dx.doi.org/10.13039/501100001809`) is that id; a placeholder (`#`, `funder%20id`) is not minted. | 431 | 0 | 11 | 129 |
| R16 | Each fundingReference is a record-scoped `dcite:FundingReference` with `dcite:funder` and `dcite:funderName`; the shared funder IRI carries no name. | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| R17 | A DOI written with `%XX` escapes (or double-encoded `%25XX`) is kept as written and counted, never decoded: DataCite registers DOIs with literal escapes. | 0 | 0 | 393,842 | 0 |
| R18 | One `dcite:PidRelation` per PID Links event, `<{subject}/event/{uuid}>`, with one subject, object, type, source and time; an event in both files is taken from May 2025. | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| R19 | A creator's name (`dcite:creatorName`), affiliations, ROR and unminted ids are on the record's `dcite:AgentRole`; an orcid.org agent carries only `dcite:orcid`. | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |

For R9 and R10, *Dropped* counts metadata **rows** not converted because a newer row of the same DOI was (no DOI is lost); for R7, *Rescued* counts relation edges that use a property this build added.

R7 in numbers: 20,048,535 relation edges now use one of the properties added in this build (they were dropped, or for links folded into `isRelatedTo`, before); 48,111 link events carry a type outside the DataCite 4.6 vocabulary and are `dcite:isRelatedTo` with their exact type on the `dcite:PidRelation`.

R3 routes: 770,898 ROR, 85,070,414 Crossref Funder ID / DOI, 1,420,053 name-minted; 87,261,365 funding references. R18: 613,426,158 PidRelations, one per event; 147,376,015 2023 events are the same uuid as a May 2025 event. R19: 107,568,498 creator roles held by an orcid.org agent, 275,686,388 by a record-local one.
R0: 28,574 DOIs that are not plain ASCII were re-keyed and checked: no two registered DOIs share an IRI; 6 registered DOIs that R1 would rewrite keep their own IRI.
The full per-file tally, with examples of every rescued, kept and dropped shape, is `datacite.tally.json` beside this file.
## Not converted

Related identifiers that are not DOI-typed (URL, Handle, ISSN, arXiv, PMID, …), descriptions/abstracts, typed dates, rights, contributors other than creators, geo locations, sizes and formats are in the Parquet but not in this graph.
## Build

`parquet_to_nt.py emit | rete build - --strict --memory-budget-mb`, so the build refuses any IRI the N-Triples grammar or RFC 3987 rejects; every emitted statement was also parsed by Oxigraph 0.5.11 before the build. Ontology `dcite:` 1.2.0 (`https://w3id.org/rete/datacite#`, OWL 2 QL-safe) travels in the file. No pyramid at this scale: keep queries selective.
